items.title: Martin Romualdez pleads not guilty to plunder; case moves to trial
items.description: Romualdez, whom the Office of the Ombudsman called the alleged 'central figure' in the flood control scheme, was charged with plunder on September 7 for allegedly receiving kickbacks

items.title: Where are we now in Rodrigo Duterte’s ICC case?
items.description: Duterte's trial will begin on November 30, but a lot of things have happened and are happening before his historic appearance at the ICC trial chamber

items.title: US admission of orbital weapons seen as landmark moment in race with China, Russia
items.description: The US, China, and Russia have raced for years to build and deploy an array of satellite networks and maneuverable spacecraft bearing capabilities that could be used to attack or tamper with other spacecraft

items.title: No single party gets majority of first-ever elected Bangsamoro Parliament
items.description: The BFP, with 31 winning bets, only has a marginal lead over rival UBJP's 30 seats. To secure a 41-seat majority, alliances with other elected parties will be key.

items.description: Rappler brings live updates, analysis, and commentary from reporters and experts as the historic impeachment trial unfolds

items.title: Remulla says Roque asylum bid denied; Roque disputes claim
items.description: Two contradicting claims, yet no proof bared just yet.

items.title: Ex-Duterte vlogger RJ Nieto gets Palace assistant secretary post
items.description: Former pro-Duterte vlogger Rey Joseph “RJ” Nieto, who was behind the now-unpublished Thinking Pinoy blog, has been appointed assistant secretary at the Office of the Cabinet Secretary.

items.description: Follow the trial, in context and in real time.

items.title: Scams, other cybercrimes rise to record 8% of families, says SWS
items.description: One in 12 Filipino families had a member fall victim to cybercrime in the past 6 months.

items.title: Duterte due in ICC courtroom to assess if fit for murder trial
items.description: Judges will hear arguments about his health and ability to stand trial, which is scheduled to begin in November. His lawyers have argued that he suffers from cognitive decline and is not well enough.

items.title: Why ABS-CBN is still retrenching 200 employees with P6 billion on the way
items.description: The new money repairs what the company owes. The retrenchment is aimed at a different problem.

items.title: Billions on paper: How much of Luzon Corridor’s $20-B pipeline will become real?
items.description: Rappler worked with an independent research analyst to see how much of the Luzon Economic Corridor pipeline is actually moving from pitch to pavement, and found that most of it is still in the planning stage

items.title: Lapid: No official has filed a truly honest SALN?
items.description: In an interjection rarely seen, Sen. Lito Lapid yesterday took the podium to bare what he called a reality in the filing of statements of assets, liabilities and net worth: no politician has ever submitted an honest declaration of his or her wealth in the SALN.

items.title: Remulla to block Zaldy’s asylum bid in France
items.description: Interior Secretary Jonvic Remulla will block former lawmaker Zaldy Co’s asylum bid in his upcoming visit to France.

items.title: Fuel excise tax relief imminent
items.description: Energy Secretary Sharon Garin has certified that the average price of Dubai crude oil in the past month breached the $80-per-barrel threshold, paving the way for the suspension of excise tax on fuel products.

items.title: Ferry June Aster captain surfaces, faces PCG
items.description: Five days after a fire struck the passenger and cargo ship MV June Aster, its captain, Roel Sarmiento, showed up at the Philippine Coast Guard’s Palawan field office yesterday to shed light on the incident that claimed 76 lives.

items.title: Congress urged: Permanently remove system loss charge
items.description: It’s now the turn of Congress – the Senate and the House of Representatives – to do its part in giving relief to consumers burdened by high electricity bills, by passing a law that would permanently remove the system loss charges, Rep. Arthur Yap of Murang Kuryente party-list said yesterday.

items.title: ICC judges urged to declare Duterte fit for trial
items.description: The prosecutor of the International Criminal Court has urged the judges handling the crimes against humanity case against former president Rodrigo Duterte to declare him fit to stand trial.
